Every road leads to a dead end. “Where am I supposed to go?” a Palestinian man cries after Israeli occupation warplanes flattened his house and workshop near the Jordanian Hospital in Gaza City’s Tel al-Hawa neighbourhood. Nothing reached his family for free, he says. Not the tent, not the tarps, not even the water jugs. They paid for all of it, scraping the money together while living in a tent, and now the strike has taken what little they had left. The UN-led Shelter Cluster says Gaza needs around 121,000 tents, 561,000 tarps and 1.7 million mattresses to get through winter, yet as of November 5 there were only about 2,800 tents, 76,000 tarps and fewer than 5,000 mattresses inside the Strip, and not a single emergency shelter kit. More than 150,000 tents are sitting outside Gaza waiting for the Israeli occupation’s approval, and the International Organization for Migration says its shelter kits keep being turned away at the crossings as “dual-use” items. Supplies cover barely 17 percent of winter shelter needs, and Save the Children says winter clothing covers just 1 percent. While families wait for aid that never comes, the airstrikes keep coming. @khaled.sulttan

Naji Abu Awad, a Palestinian American based in Texas, returned to his hometown of Turmus’ayya in the occupied West Bank to take back his family home after Israeli soldiers broke in and occupied it for more than two weeks, turning it into a military outpost. When Naji arrived, Israeli soldiers confronted him with guns and smoke grenades. Imagine being unable to leave your home because Israeli soldiers or settlers might use your absence to take it from you. For Palestinians across the occupied West Bank, that fear is part of daily life. Home theft, settler attacks, and forced displacement are not isolated incidents. They are part of a system designed to make Palestinian life increasingly impossible while expanding Israeli control over Palestinian land.

PLEASE TAKE A MOMENT TO READ MY STORY… 😢💔 Last night, once again, I survived. I survived another frightening night in Gaza, and I am deeply grateful to God for keeping me and my family alive. 🤲 As a nurse, I have witnessed pain, suffering, and heartbreaking situations that words can never fully explain. I have seen patients struggling without medicine, families going hungry, and people desperately searching for the most basic necessities of life. Despite everything my family and I have been through, I made a decision: I could not stand by and watch others suffer without trying to help. That is why I started caring for patients and vulnerable families, providing basic necessities such as food, medicine, and financial assistance whenever possible. I continue working without receiving a salary. I do this because I believe every human life matters, and I cannot abandon the people who need care and compassion. My dear friends, please, I beg you: listen to our cries for help. Our patients and families are still struggling. They need food, medicine, and someone willing to stand beside them. We cannot do this alone. 😭🙏 One more thing: For my personal safety, I have chosen not to show my face in this video. Please do not share or repost it. This video is intended for documentation purposes only. Thank you to everyone who listens, cares, and remembers us in their prayers. May God protect every innocent life and reward every kind heart. 🤲❤️
